body: I'm having a look at this one.
Outch, this is a Pandora box :). I'm very surprised we didn't have ton of small issues because of that.

Hum, yeah... I've tried a few things, but I'm blocked on AsciiString (which needs a substitution for the constructor, but at the same time have static methods accessing the constructor (and this is not supported by GraalVM)).
The runtime initialization is not going to work or will be very expensive. Substituting the PlatformDependent class sounds a lot better.
@gsmet Sorry, to bump this issue again, but i think it is quite relevant. Cause this makes runtime memory settings dependent on the build machine.
Would be great to have an update reproducer, as I never encountered the issue.
@antonwiens can you attach a sample application using one of the latest Quarkus versions that behaves like you mention?

> @antonwiens can you attach a sample application using one of the latest Quarkus versions that behaves like you mention?


I looked at the PlatformDependent and PooledByteBufAllocator class code of the current version of netty, which still initializes the maxDirectMemory in static variables and gets defined during native image build time. thats why it will use max direct memory from the native image build time environment and not the runtime environment, this creating buffers and pools using the wrong maxdirectmemory from build time and not runtime.
The natve-image properties of netty don't include a platformdependent and there are no substitutes there, so it should still exist.


I will create a reproducer, but i have little time and it may take a while till i come to it.
I hope the reproducer will clarify this.
@antonwiens did you have any luck with the reproducer?
